Let me try to understand the chemical principles involved in this problem. The wavenumber (frequency) of the carbonyl stretching mode is affected by the electron-withdrawing or electron-donating properties of the adjacent groups.

The more electron-withdrawing the group attached to the carbonyl, the higher the wavenumber of the C=O stretch. This is because electron-withdrawing groups increase the bond order of the C=O bond by resonance or inductive effects.

For halogens, the electronegativity order is:
F > Cl > Br > I

The more electronegative the halogen, the more electron-withdrawing it is. In these compounds, we have trihalomethyl groups (CF₃, CCl₃, CBr₃, CI₃) attached to the carbonyl.

The electron-withdrawing ability follows the same trend as electronegativity:
CF₃ > CCl₃ > CBr₃ > CI₃

Therefore, the wavenumber of the carbonyl stretching mode should increase in the order:
CI₃ < CBr₃ < CCl₃ < CF₃

Looking at our options:
A. CBr₃ < CI₃ < CF₃ (incorrect order for CI₃)
B. CCl₃ < CF₃ < CI₃ (incorrect order for CI₃)
C. CF₃ < CI₃ < CCl₃ (incorrect order for both CI₃ and CCl₃)
D. CI₃ < CCl₃ < CF₃ (correct order based on electronegativity)

Based on the electronegativity trend and its effect on carbonyl stretching frequency, the correct answer is D.
